correctness.rationale: The boundary-support lemma is proved in both directions from the canonical chain neighborhoods. The weight enumerator then follows by an exhaustive disjoint partition according to whether label 2 occurs on neither side, only A, only B, or both sides, with extremal 2-class indices determining exactly which classes may contain 0 or 2. A direct adjacency-level verifier checks all 3,023,307 labelings over all 255 positive canonical profiles of order at most 9 and agrees on the criterion, every polynomial coefficient, and the minimum weight.

value.rationale: The result converts the global isolate-free positive-support constraint into two extreme-class positivity tests and thereby produces an exact all-weight enumerator on a canonical graph class. This strictly refines the minimum parameter, provides counts at every weight, and gives a natural structured-class counterpart to the known bipartite hardness of total Roman domination.
